$comment: Presentation overlay for task_spec.v1.json. Labels, units, groups and widget
kinds -- everything a form needs that a JSON Schema deliberately does not carry.
IT CHANGES NOTHING ABOUT COMPILATION. No pass reads this file; taskgraph/
presentation.py loads it and nothing else imports that module. It lives here
rather than in the consuming app for one reason: a field added to the schema
needs a label the same day, and a table in another repo is a mirror with
nothing keeping it in sync. tests/test_presentation_covers_schema.py is what
makes that concrete -- it walks every leaf in the schema and fails if the
overlay does not name it, and fails again for a key naming nothing.
KEYS ARE NORMALISED DIAGNOSTIC LOCATIONS. `timing[].ms` and
diagnostic onto the field that caused it is a dictionary lookup rather than a
parser. Note that `contingency.stimuli` and `contingency.trial_types` are YAML
arrays whose diagnostics address them BY ID, so they take `*` and not `[]`.

groups.label: Identity
groups.help: What this spec is called and which frozen contracts it pins.

groups.label: Topology
groups.help: The only layer that changes the graph. Every other layer fills the shape these knobs produce.

groups.label: Timing
groups.help: One duration per id. Order is load-bearing: the index is what the firmware holds.

groups.label: Context schedule
groups.help: Reversals. Which target a trial type maps to, from a given trial onward.

groups.label: Outcomes
groups.help: Which trigger routes to which terminal. This is where go/no-go's inversion lives.

groups.label: Stage schedule
groups.help: Shaping ramps. The board applies ONE row -- the latest whose trial count has been reached.

spec_version.label: Spec version
spec_version.help: Always 1. Bumping it is a schema change, not an edit.

spec_id.label: Spec id
spec_id.help: Lowercase, underscores. It is the filename, the table's identity, and half of what a board reports back after an upload.

vocab_version.label: Vocabulary version
vocab_version.help: Which strobe registry this spec's names resolve against.

meta.label.label: Name
meta.label.help: What the library shows. Free text -- it names nothing on disk, so changing it is safe at any time.

meta.description.label: Description
meta.description.help: What this task measures. Never affects compilation, but IS covered by the spec hash, so an edit here is visible in the session record.

meta.reproduces_sketch.label: Reproduces sketch
meta.reproduces_sketch.help: Names the hand-written sketch this spec must match strobe-for-strobe. Its presence is what makes this an equivalence target.

meta.derived_from.label: Derived from
meta.derived_from.help: Another spec id this one is a delta of. Documentation only -- nothing is inherited.

topology.template.label: Template
topology.template.help: Which epoch template emits the graph. Task authors never write a node.

topology.template_version.label: Template version
topology.template_version.help: Versioned by file and never edited once pinned, so changing this re-derives the whole graph.

topology.n_sampling_stages.label: Sampling stages
topology.n_sampling_stages.help: How many stimuli the subject samples in sequence before answering. 0 skips the sampling epoch entirely.

topology.retention_delay.label: Retention delay
topology.retention_delay.help: Insert a delay between the last stimulus and the response window.

topology.response_mode.label: Response mode
topology.response_mode.help: What counts as answering. The interpreter never branches on this -- both modes are expressed by which outcome classes carry which edge effects, which is why 'correct = timeout' needs no special case.

options.label: N-alternative
options.help: Entry into the target port is correct; entry elsewhere is wrong.

options.label: Go / no-go
options.help: Success is defined by inaction -- the window expiring is the correct outcome, and any entry is a false alarm.

topology.response_ports.label: Response ports
topology.response_ports.help: Which declared ports the response window watches.

topology.commit_hold.label: Commitment hold
topology.commit_hold.help: Require the subject to hold at the engagement port before the first stimulus is delivered.

topology.cue_off_placement.label: Cue-off placement
topology.cue_off_placement.help: Template v1 only; v2 dropped the knob.

timing[].id.label: Id
timing[].id.help: Referenced by name everywhere. Renaming one breaks every reference to it, which the compiler catches.

timing[].ms.label: Duration
timing[].ms.help: How long the states holding this id dwell. Capped at 32767: firmware stores timings as a signed int and uses 32767 itself as the 'never' sentinel.

timing[].wire_key.label: START token
timing[].wire_key.help: The legacy START parameter this duration corresponds to. Two ids sharing a token with different values is a warning, because the legacy path can only supply one number.

timing[].note.label: Note
timing[].note.help: Why this duration is what it is -- usually the firmware field it mirrors. An edit that changes what the note describes should delete it rather than leave a citation that is no longer true.

contingency.stimuli.*.id.label: Id
contingency.stimuli.*.id.help: How trial types refer to this stimulus. Renaming it breaks every stage that names it.

contingency.stimuli.*.emitter.label: Emitter
contingency.stimuli.*.emitter.help: Which actuator line delivers it. A stimulus is an emitter channel and nothing more, so a speaker or an LED substitutes for an odour valve without any change to the model.

contingency.stimuli.*.on_code.label: Onset strobe
contingency.stimuli.*.on_code.help: Marks the moment the stimulus reaches the subject, not when it was primed.

contingency.stimuli.*.note.label: Note
contingency.stimuli.*.note.help: Free text for whoever reads this spec next. Never compiled.

contingency.ports.*.channel.label: Channel
contingency.ports.*.channel.help: Which input channel this port is. Named, never numbered -- Rig wiring says which pin the name is on, so re-wiring a box changes no spec.

contingency.ports.*.enter_code.label: Enter strobe
contingency.ports.*.enter_code.help: Recorded the instant the subject enters this port, BEFORE correctness is known -- the poke is an event in its own right, not a verdict.

contingency.ports.*.error_code.label: Error strobe
contingency.ports.*.error_code.help: Recorded when entering this port is the wrong answer. A withhold task never reports one, which is why switching to n-alternative makes this field reachable and required.

contingency.ports.*.break_code.label: Break strobe
contingency.ports.*.break_code.help: Recorded when the subject reaches this port but releases before the response hold completes -- a consummatory failure, not a wrong choice.

contingency.ports.*.exit_code.label: Exit strobe
contingency.ports.*.exit_code.help: Recorded when the subject withdraws. On a rewarded port this is the only place the end of a consummatory bout is observed.

contingency.ports.*.reward_line.label: Reward line
contingency.ports.*.reward_line.help: Absent means this port never rewards -- the template then emits no reward or consumption node for it at all.

contingency.ports.*.reward_duration.label: Reward duration
contingency.ports.*.reward_duration.help: Pulse width IS delivered volume. This is the one duration resolved per trial rather than from the timing vector.

contingency.ports.*.reward_code.label: Reward strobe
contingency.ports.*.reward_code.help: Recorded as the reward line opens. Paired with the reward-stop code, the two bracket the delivery in the data file.

contingency.ports.*.reward_stop_code.label: Reward-stop strobe
contingency.ports.*.reward_stop_code.help: Recorded as the reward line closes, colocated with the actuator change rather than bracketed around it.

contingency.ports.*.note.label: Note
contingency.ports.*.note.help: Free text for whoever reads this spec next. Never compiled.

contingency.trial_types.*.id.label: Id
contingency.trial_types.*.id.help: Names this trial type in the context schedule and in the data. It is what an analysis groups by, so renaming one splits its history.

contingency.trial_types.*.stages.label: Stimuli
contingency.trial_types.*.stages.help: Exactly one entry per sampling stage -- that is what makes the stage-indexed binding resolvable.

contingency.trial_types.*.target.label: Correct port
contingency.trial_types.*.target.help: Null is the withhold declaration: with no correct port, no entry can satisfy the target guard.

contingency.trial_types.*.weight.label: Weight
contingency.trial_types.*.weight.help: How often this type is drawn, relative to the others. 0 keeps it in the pool but never presents it, which is how a shaping ramp turns an arm on later. Ignored where selection is live (anti-bias).

contingency.trial_types.*.note.label: Note
contingency.trial_types.*.note.help: Free text for whoever reads this spec next. Never compiled.

contingency.context_schedule[].at_trial.label: From trial
contingency.context_schedule[].at_trial.help: The trial count this row takes over at. The board applies ONE row -- the latest whose count has been reached.

contingency.context_schedule[].context.label: Context
contingency.context_schedule[].context.help: A name for this block, recorded so an analysis can tell a reversal's halves apart.

contingency.context_schedule[].targets.*.label: Target
contingency.context_schedule[].targets.*.help: Which port is correct for this trial type from here on, overriding the trial type's own. A reversal is entirely this -- no state, edge or duration moves.

contingency.outcome_map.*.trigger.label: Trigger
contingency.outcome_map.*.trigger.help: Which edge event scores this outcome. Inverting one is how go/no-go makes a timeout correct.

contingency.outcome_map.*.terminal.label: Terminal
contingency.outcome_map.*.terminal.help: How the trial is counted. INVALID trials are re-presented and do not advance the counter.

contingency.outcome_map.*.delay.label: Delay
contingency.outcome_map.*.delay.help: The interval that runs before the trial closes -- an ITI on a good outcome, a penalty on a bad one.

contingency.outcome_map.*.reward.label: Reward
contingency.outcome_map.*.reward.help: A port name, `@target` for whichever port this trial's type nominates, or null for no reward.

contingency.outcome_map.*.strobe.label: Strobe
contingency.outcome_map.*.strobe.help: Explicit null means a deliberately silent transition, which is invisible in the record. That is different from omitting the key.

contingency.outcome_map.*.note.label: Note
contingency.outcome_map.*.note.help: Why this ending is classified the way it is. Free text for whoever reads this spec next; never compiled.

policy.selection.mode.label: Mode
policy.selection.mode.help: How the next trial type is drawn. None of this changes the machine -- selection runs before a trial starts and the graph is the same either way.

options.label: Weighted pool
options.help: Independent draws in proportion to weight.

options.label: Block shuffled
options.help: Each block holds every trial type in its declared proportion, shuffled.

options.label: Anti-bias
options.help: Reweights against a side the subject has been favouring, over a rolling window.

policy.selection.block_size.label: Block size
policy.selection.block_size.help: How many trials one shuffled block holds. Each block carries every trial type in its declared proportion, so the sides stay balanced over the block rather than only in expectation.

policy.selection.bias_window.label: Bias window
policy.selection.bias_window.help: How many recent responses the bias estimate covers.

policy.selection.debias_strength.label: Debias strength
policy.selection.debias_strength.help: How hard to push back against a side the subject has been favouring. 0 leaves the draw alone; 1 corrects the observed bias fully.

policy.selection.p_min.label: Min probability
policy.selection.p_min.help: Floor on any one side's draw probability. With the ceiling it stops de-biasing collapsing into a deterministic -- and therefore cueable -- alternation.

policy.selection.p_max.label: Max probability
policy.selection.p_max.help: Ceiling on any one side's draw probability, so a strongly biased subject is never fed one side exclusively.

policy.selection.max_run.label: Max run
policy.selection.max_run.help: Longest run of one trial type before the next draw is forced to differ.

policy.correction.budgets.*.label: Budget
policy.correction.budgets.*.help: How many correction trials a wrong answer at this port may earn. 0 disables correction for it.

policy.penalty_escalation.applies_to.label: Applies to
policy.penalty_escalation.applies_to.help: Which outcome class lengthens its delay on repetition.

policy.penalty_escalation.step_ms.label: Step
policy.penalty_escalation.step_ms.help: How much longer the penalty gets each time it repeats without being cleared.

policy.penalty_escalation.ceiling_ms.label: Ceiling
policy.penalty_escalation.ceiling_ms.help: The longest the escalated penalty can grow to, however many times it repeats.

policy.penalty_escalation.clears_on.label: Clears on
policy.penalty_escalation.clears_on.help: What resets the escalator. MUST be declared, never implied: a bare poke that does not complete a trial must not defuse an abstention penalty, and the loophole has been reopened once already by a copy-paste.

options.label: Any engagement
options.help: Clearing on engagement alone lets a subject reset the penalty without ever answering.

policy.penalty_escalation.arm_after_stag.label: Arm after stage
policy.penalty_escalation.arm_after_stag.help: Escalation only arms once this stage row is live. An eased task points it at the last row, so an animal still being shaped is never escalated against.

policy.stage_schedule[].at_trial.label: From trial
policy.stage_schedule[].at_trial.help: The trial count this row takes over at. The board applies ONE row -- the latest whose count has been reached -- so rows do not accumulate.

policy.stage_schedule[].set.*.label: New value
policy.stage_schedule[].set.*.help: Every row must restate every timing entry the schedule touches -- an omitted entry keeps whatever it had, which is not necessarily the previous row's value.

policy.n_trials.label: Trials
policy.n_trials.help: How many trials the session runs before it ends itself. Only trials that ADVANCE count -- an invalid trial is re-presented and does not move the counter.

policy.seed.label: Seed
policy.seed.help: `host` lets the app draw one per run from the OS CSPRNG, which is what makes two sessions unlikely to share a trial order. A literal integer is for reproducing one.
